subject: Clarify: default capture windows and KV-cache vs final outputs (MedLytix compliance)
messages:
From: Ingrid Lin <ingrid.lin@medlytix.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, security@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Data capture details for HIPAA review

Hi Kimberly / Redwood security team,

Thanks again for the time earlier. MedLytix is doing a HIPAA gap assessment and we have a couple of specific questions about what is captured by default from API traffic. Please confirm as precisely as you can because our compliance team will rely on the language. Key items: 

1) Streaming fragments: when a response is streamed back to a client (partial tokens), are those fragments ever persisted to disk or to long-term logs by default? If so, what is the default retention and the deletion workflow?

2) KV cache and session state: does Redwood persist KV cache snapshots or session-level token caches beyond an active session? If yes — where and for how long?

3) Prompts and user inputs vs model outputs: what is stored by default for hosted customers? Are prompts treated differently from model-generated outputs and do they have different retention horizons?

4) Backups/audit archives: do backups / analytics extracts include raw prompts or only aggregated metadata? How do we provide proof-of-deletion for a given customer (MedLytix) if required by a regulator?

I attached our questionnaire (MedLytix_Security_Questionnaire_v2.docx) for completeness. Happy to hop on a short call if needed.

Best,
Ingrid
Director, Security & Compliance
MedLytix

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Ingrid Lin <ingrid.lin@medlytix.com>
Cc: security@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data capture details for HIPAA review

Hi Ingrid — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, high-confidence summary and next steps. I also attached a short retention summary PDF for quick reference.

Short answers (high level):
- Streaming fragments: transient only. Streaming buffers are held in-memory and in transient buffers for request processing; by default we do NOT persist partial token fragments to long-term storage. The buffer is kept for the duration of the request (typical <2 minutes) and is not part of the default log store.
- KV cache / session state: KV caches are per-model-session and treated as ephemeral in our hosted environment. They are not checkpointed into our long-term request/response store unless the customer enables session replay or explicitly requests session export.
- Prompts vs outputs: for hosted customers the default capture window includes full request payloads (prompts) and final model outputs for 45 days to support troubleshooting and abuse review; prompts and outputs are stored together in the request/response index and subject to the same retention by default.
- Backups & analytics: periodic analytics/aggregates exclude full prompt text by default (only hashed identifiers and metadata). Backups of the request/response datastore are covered by the same retention rules — raw payloads are not kept longer than configured retention unless a customer has an extended retention contract.

Next steps: Jonas and Laura — can you confirm the KV-cache persistence language and the proof-of-deletion artifact we provide (deletion manifest / tombstone id + storage snapshot) so I can give Ingrid the final wording for their documentation team?

Kimberly
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_retention_summary.pdf

Forwarding MedLytix thread — they need definitive language for their SOC/HIPAA pack. Please confirm the technical details below so I can respond formally:

- Confirm: streaming fragments are never written to persistent blob storage in hosted mode (only short-lived buffers).
- Confirm: KV cache snapshots: ephemeral by default; do we ever write them to S3/EBS for debugging auto-collection? If so, under what trigger and retention window?
- Proof-of-deletion: what is the minimal artifact we can hand to a customer to show full removal of their request/response records (requested format: deletion-id + timestamp + list of shard locations or archive names).

Quoted message included below.

On Sat, Apr 25, 2026 at 12:15 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Ingrid — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, high-confidence summary and next steps....

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ingrid Lin <ingrid.lin@medlytix.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Apr 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Data capture details for HIPAA review

Kimberly / team / Ingrid — confirmed details below (technical owner perspective). Feel free to pull any of this into a customer-friendly statement.

1) Streaming fragments: confirmed transient-only. Streams are assembled in-memory and in a short-lived buffer; we do not persist partial streams to disk in our hosted environment. The buffer lifetime is request-scoped and is typically cleared within seconds to a few minutes after completion. There are two exceptions (both opt-in/explicit):
  - Customer-enabled session replay: when a customer opts in to capture session replay for debugging, we checkpoint session fragments to a transient blob (S3) for a configurable short window (default 7 days) before automatic purge. This is not on by default.
  - Internal debug snapshots: in rare incident response, an engineer may trigger a secure snapshot which is written to an internal-only, access-controlled bucket; such snapshots are logged and their retention is 30 days unless an exception is approved by SRE and Security.

2) KV cache / session state: the KV cache is in-memory and not materialized to our standard request/response store by default. We do maintain very short-lived checkpointing for long-running sessions when the model runtime requires it (e.g., very large contexts) — those checkpoints are stored encrypted on ephemeral storage, not in our long-term index, and are removed within 24 hours. We do NOT persist KV-cache contents into backups/archives unless a customer explicitly requests session export or enables a feature that requires session persistence.

3) Prompts and outputs retention: hosted default is 45 days for raw request/response payloads (both prompt text and final outputs). This aligns with our standard troubleshooting/abuse SLO and is configurable via customer settings or enterprise contracts. For customers requiring shorter windows we provide auto-purge options (e.g., immediate erasure on request for dedicated/private plans) and for longer-term audit needs we offer a signed-archival path under contract.

4) Backups & proof-of-deletion: our deletion workflow produces a deletion manifest (deletion-id, timestamp, affected shards/objects) and an irreversible tombstone marker in the index. For a compliance request we provide a signed manifest + storage snapshot id and a short runbook describing the wipe steps. Where applicable (enterprise/private), we can include a notarized audit log entry showing the deletion event.

Bottom line for MedLytix (customer-facing):
- Default: streamed fragments are transient-only; prompts + final outputs are retained 45 days by default in hosted.
- KV cache is ephemeral and not part of long-term logs unless explicitly enabled.
- Proof-of-deletion: we provide a deletion manifest + signed timestamp; enterprise plans can request notarized evidence.

Jonas Weber
Senior Infra Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
